newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger, 30-year at new high.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger, 30-year at new high.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday, as the price of the 30-year bond reached an all-time high, forcing many traders to cover short positions, analysts said.

"It was the U.S. (gains) as much as anything," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "Inevitably on the upticks we tend to outperform the U.S. because each time we make a new high like today we squeeze a new round of shorts."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.68 to C$121.25 to yield 6.395 percent.
The Canadian 30-year is at the highest price and lowest yield since its inception.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 9/32 to yield 6.38 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to two basis points from four basis points at Monday's close.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets initially opened weaker after the U.S. Labor Department said the employment cost index for the second quarter rose 0.8 percent, in line with expectations. But the U.S. market turned negative by midday, taking the Canadian market with it and catching many Canadian traders short.

Dealers said that even with portions of the market at record highs, reduced supply was compelling many investors to maintain long positions, forcing traders who had placed short trades to pay up to cover their positions.

"This is still a technically sound bond market and market technicians are calling for higher prices and lower yields," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.34 to C$110.13 to yield 5.877 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.11 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 23 basis points from 21 basis points at Monday's close.
